The spec's Touch points (docs/specs/ytdlp-node-runtime.md:239-268) name no file under addons/intelligence/tests/. The change is test-only scope drift. It supports the I5 test, which needs a successful lookup that also writes to stderr.

providers/youtube.py:57 adds a module-level `from ...service import JS_RUNTIME_OPTIONS`. Lines 262 and 271 keep the lazy imports inside functions. manager.py:37-38 already imported ..service at module level. service.py:35 is its only module-level relative import (.schemas), and it does not import subscription, so the new import makes no circular import. The import graph does widen: importing the provider now loads service and its app.* imports (service.py:20-33). This is outside the literal touch point but has no behavioral defect I could find.

specification_compliance: The four findings are scope observations about files outside the Touch points list. All are test files or an import-graph change; none contradicts a declared invariant.

JS_RUNTIME_OPTIONS = {'js_runtimes': {'node': {}}} (service.py:44) is spread into options dicts at service.py:83,171,271,344, manager.py:99 and providers/youtube.py:192,219. That is seven sites, matching the seven dicts in I3/I4.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Importing subscription/providers/youtube.py now loads media_import's service module and its app.* dependencies at import time. Before, that happened only when a function that needs service was called.
regression_risks: A test or tool that imports providers.youtube in an environment where service's app.* imports cannot load would now fail at import. I did not check whether any existing test depends on that.
test_coverage: The I5 test path relies on the new stderr knob in the shared fake yt-dlp. Existing callers of set_ytdlp keep their behavior because stderr defaults to None, which the script treats as falsy.
